$description: per-proposed-id provenance the ruling record has no slot for.

s272-D1.label: How many primary buttons per what — and what is the 'what'?

quotes.IBM Carbon: Primary buttons should only appear once per screen
quotes.Atlassian: Only include one primary button or call to action (CTA) in a page
quotes.Fluent 2: Only use one primary button in a layout for the most important action.
quotes.Ant Design: there can be at most one primary button in a section.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Don't use more than one primary button in a section or screen
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: Don't use more than 3 accent buttons in the same view.
quotes.GOV.UK: silent on count
quotes.USWDS: Avoid using too many buttons on a page.
quotes.NN/g: Primary buttons have the most visual emphasis to grab user attention
quotes.OURS: button.meta antiPatterns[0]: 'Using more than one primary button in a single context' — 'context' is undefined

s272-D1.why_contested: The COUNT is near-unanimous (1) with one outlier (3). The SCOPE word is not: screen · page · layout · section · view. No gate can check 'context'.
options: One primary per SCREEN (Carbon's word) — strictest, catches a primary in a card inside a page that already has one.
One primary per SECTION (Ant/Polaris) — allows a page-level primary plus one per card or panel.
One primary per LAYOUT REGION as defined by our app-shell (page header · main · action bar · each modal surface) — our own vocabulary rather than an imported one.
Leave 'context' undefined and keep the rule advisory.
s272-D1.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. It is the only wording that names things our library already has, so a gate can walk the DOM and count. Carbon's 'screen' is the closest external match and explicitly excludes the app header, modal and side panel — which is option 3 in different words.

s272-D2.label: Can a LINK perform an action (download a PDF, open a new window), or must that be a button?
s272-D2.chosen_option: Links navigate only. A download becomes a button, and document-row / links / footer all change.

quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use links for actions that will change data
quotes.Atlassian: Links navigate to a new page or anchor location, changing the URL.
quotes.Fluent 2: Don't use links for triggering actions other than navigation.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Links are used primarily for navigation
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: Buttons allow users to perform an action or to navigate to another page.
quotes.GOV.UK: silent on the boundary (its Button page covers 'Start now' links styled as buttons)
quotes.USWDS: silent on the boundary
quotes.NN/g: not obtained — the two article slugs tried both 404 (see SOURCES refused)
quotes.OURS: links.meta purpose: 'navigate between pages/content items or instigate actions (e.g. download pdf, open in a new window)'

s272-D2.why_contested: Four systems fence links to navigation only. Spectrum crosses the line the other way (buttons may navigate). OUR OWN META crosses it in the direction four systems forbid, and 'download pdf' is a real, frequent HSBC case — every document row in the library depends on the answer.
options: Links navigate only. A download becomes a button, and document-row / links / footer all change.
Links navigate AND fetch a resource (download, open-in-new-window) but never mutate state — a narrower crossing than our meta currently allows, and the one a URL actually justifies.
Keep our meta as written and record that we knowingly diverge from Carbon, Atlassian, Fluent and Polaris.
s272-D2.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 2. A download IS a navigation to a URL; it changes nothing on the server. That keeps our existing arrow/icon links legal, keeps the four systems' actual concern (mutation) satisfied, and gives a gate a checkable clause: a link may not be bound to a handler that mutates.

s272-D3.label: Is a tooltip REQUIRED on an icon-only button?

quotes.Atlassian: Use tooltips with icon buttons to display the button label.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Be provided for icon-only buttons or a button with an associated keyboard shortcut.
quotes.USWDS: Tooltips are useful as a last resort for space-constrained UI.
quotes.Material 3: They're best used for labelling UI elements with no text
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on the requirement
quotes.OURS: icon-button.meta antiPatterns[3]: 'Using an ambiguous glyph as the only action affordance without a tooltip/label' — 'tooltip/label', i.e. either

s272-D3.why_contested: Two systems make it a requirement, two describe it as the tooltip's main purpose, ours makes it one of two acceptable options and only for AMBIGUOUS glyphs. The accessible name is separately mandatory in all of them — this row is about the VISIBLE label only.
options: Tooltip required on every icon-only button. Gateable, and it would fail real screens today.
Tooltip required only where the glyph is not in the agreed universal set (close, search, add, edit, download) — which is exactly the set roles.json already invokes with 'the glyph is universal'.
Keep our either/or wording.
s272-D3.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 2. It uses a fence roles.json already has, it is checkable against a named glyph list, and it avoids putting a tooltip on a close × that nobody has ever misread.

s272-D4.label: How many actions in an action bar, and which side are they on?

quotes.IBM Carbon: Any more than three actions should be grouped
quotes.Ant Design: more than three operations, you can group some of them into a Dropdown
quotes.GOV.UK: aligned to the left so users do not miss it
quotes.Fluent 2: Optional footer, which can contain up to three actions.
quotes.OURS: action-bar.meta antiPatterns[0] (REVIEW, inferred): 'more than ~3 actions in the bar'; drawer.meta antiPatterns[2]: 'Right-aligned actions (family order is primary-first, left-aligned)'

s272-D4.why_contested: The CEILING is effectively unanimous at 3 (Carbon, Ant, Fluent, and our own guess) — so the count is not the contest. The ALIGNMENT is: GOV.UK and our own Drawer say left, primary first; our Action-bar meta warns about DOM order in a way that assumes a right-aligned pair.
options: Left-aligned, primary first, everywhere — matching our Drawer rule and GOV.UK.
Right-aligned in modals and drawers (platform convention), left-aligned in page-level action bars.
Leave alignment to the surface and gate only the DOM order.
s272-D4.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1, and promote the ~3 ceiling from a REVIEW guess to a ruled number — three systems independently landed on the same figure, which is as close to free as this table gets.

s272-D5.label: Is the FAB mobile-only?
s272-D5.chosen_option: Any viewport, with a rule that FAB and Back-to-top may never both be present.

quotes.Material 3: Don't display multiple FABs on a single screen
quotes.Material 3 (2): Use a FAB for the most important action on a screen
quotes.Ant Design: Buttons that can be seen wherever you browse.
quotes.IBM Carbon: no FAB component
quotes.GOV.UK: no FAB component
quotes.OURS: fab.meta: 'fixed to a mobile viewport'; mustNotNeighbour Back-to-top, collision UNRESOLVED

s272-D5.why_contested: The COUNT rule (one per screen) is unanimous among the two systems that ship it and is already ours. The PLATFORM is not: ours says mobile, Ant's float button is global and desktop. Four systems ship nothing at all. And our own meta records an unresolved collision with Back-to-top plus two raw constants (56px, 24px) awaiting your mint-or-accept.
options: Mobile-only, as built. Back-to-top wins the bottom-right corner on desktop; FAB never appears there.
Any viewport, with a rule that FAB and Back-to-top may never both be present.
FAB is removed and its job goes to the action bar or page header — which is what six of eleven systems effectively do.
s272-D5.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1, and resolve the collision by ruling that Back-to-top yields to a FAB when both would appear. The meta already flags this as yours; the predicate cannot be finished without it.

s272-D6.label: quick-actions
s272-D6.when_gate: the surface is a home or account screen AND each item is a shortcut to an existing destination or task AND every item has a visible label AND reordering has a keyboard path
s272-D6.when_prose: beats a row of buttons because the items are user-configurable shortcuts rather than the screen's own actions; beats navigations because these are tasks, not a structure; yields to action-bar whenever the actions belong to the screen's commit point rather than to the user's shortcuts.

s272-D7.label: cta-lockup

sources: Atlassian empty-state ("Include too many call to action buttons on one page")

s272-D7.when_gate: a band closes a page or section with a heading, a supporting line and EXACTLY ONE action pair (secondary + primary) AND no third button AND no invented urgency copy AND width comes from the container
s272-D7.when_prose: beats a loose button pair because the band is an arrangement with a heading that earns the action; yields to action-bar whenever the actions commit a form rather than invite a next step; the single-pair ceiling is ours (antiPatterns[3]) and is consistent with the one-primary rule five systems state for button.

s272-D8.label: May more than one accordion section be open at once?

quotes.NN/g: make sure to give people the capability to open multiple sections at a time
quotes.Ant Design: an Accordion is by definition the Collapse variant that allows only one panel expanded
quotes.GOV.UK: silent on the rule; ships a Show-all-sections control, which implies multi
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on the rule
quotes.USWDS: silent on the rule; ships both bordered and multiselectable variants
quotes.ours: silent — our meta says nothing about it

options: Multi-open is the default (NN/g, and GOV.UK's show-all control implies it).
Single-open is the default; multi is a variant.
Both are variants and the composer picks; the meta names the trade-off.
s272-D8.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. GOV.UK's Show-all-sections button only makes sense in a multi-open accordion, and we already inherit GOV.UK-shaped accordion behaviour. Ant is naming a different component with the same word.

s272-D9.label: Does Carousel stay in the library?

quotes.NN/g: some people will only see the first frame or none at all
quotes.NN/g (title): Consider Using a Hero Image Instead of a Carousel
quotes.Ant Design: When there is a group of content on the same level.
quotes.GOV.UK / USWDS / IBM Carbon / Polaris: NO CAROUSEL COMPONENT EXISTS — four systems' worth of structural silence
quotes.ours: PROPOSED #210 wave-4 lane C; not registered, not ruled; autoplay OFF proposed

options: Drop it. Four reference systems ship none and NN/g says don't.
Keep it, unratified, with a `when` written as a warning and a hard autoplay-off default.
Keep and ratify it as a normal component with a positive `when`.
s272-D9.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. It is already unratified, so nothing is lost by leaving it there with an honest negative `when` — and a fintech marketing surface will ask for one whatever we write. Option 3 is the one the evidence does not support.

s272-D10.label: Is there a maximum number of cards in a card collection?

quotes.USWDS: Consider limiting the number of items in each collection to six or fewer.
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on a number
quotes.Ant Design: silent on a number

options: Adopt 6 as a soft ceiling above which cards yield to list-items or table.
No number; yield to table on the COMPARISON test instead ("if a field is read down a column, it is a table").
Both: 6 as a warning, the comparison test as the gate.
s272-D10.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. USWDS's 6 applies to their `collection` component, not their `card` — importing it onto our Cards would be a quote lifted out of its component. The comparison test is the one that actually discriminates.

s272-D11.label: What language and furniture may an error page carry?

quotes.GOV.UK: technical jargon like 404 or bad request
quotes.USWDS: Don't use this template for form validation errors, submission errors
quotes.Ant Design: silent
quotes.NN/g: silent

options: Adopt GOV.UK's bans (no 404 jargon, no breadcrumbs, no humour) as gate clauses.
Adopt them as content guidance only, off the gate.
Adopt the no-breadcrumbs clause only — it is structural and checkable; leave tone to review.

s272-D12.label: stats-band-lockup
s272-D12.when_gate: tiles >= 2 of {stat-card, kpi-tile} AND a section heading is present AND the row auto-fills AND no new molecule is drawn
s272-D12.when_prose: the labelled row of metric tiles; beats hand-rolling the dashboard KPI section (which Template-dashboard already does) because it fixes the heading + auto-fill grid once; composes Layout-utilities, Stat-card, Kpi-tile and Cards' arrow-link ONLY — a new molecule here is an explicit do-not-rule (our AP1).

s272-D13.label: feature-grid-lockup
s272-D13.when_gate: surface = marketing AND cells >= 2 AND every cell = icon + title + body AND cells carry NO per-cell action
s272-D13.when_prose: beats cards (roles.json when: "a bordered surface per item") because a feature cell states a benefit and does not carry its own call to action — our meta removes the action row deliberately; beats layout-utilities (when: "default") because the cell CONTENT is fixed, which is the whole component.

s272-D14.label: How many series may a grouped bar chart carry?

quotes.FT Visual Vocabulary: Can become tricky to read with more than 2 series
quotes.ours (chart-line): series 1–5 on one continuous time axis
quotes.IBM Carbon: unreachable

options: Adopt 2 as a soft ceiling for grouped bars, above which use stacked or small multiples.
Adopt chart-line's 1–5 for consistency across the family.
No ceiling.
s272-D14.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2, with the FT's 2 recorded as a caution. A hard 2 would make a four-quarter grouped comparison illegal, which is a normal fintech chart; but the family should not have a 5-series line and an unbounded bar.

s272-D15.label: How many slices may a pie or donut carry?

quotes.Datawrapper: If you have more than five shares, consider a stacked column
quotes.roles.json (ours): chart-pie when: "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts"
quotes.our metas: antiPatterns[0] on BOTH pie and donut: "More than 6 slices (dv-pie-009 — combine into 'Other')"
quotes.FT Visual Vocabulary: silent on a number; "difficult to accurately compare the size of the segments"
quotes.NN/g: silent on a number; against the family entirely
quotes.IBM Carbon: unreachable (chart-types is client-rendered)

options: 5 everywhere: change dv-pie-009 to 5 and keep roles.json.
6 everywhere: change roles.json's pie `when` to ≤ 6.
Keep both on purpose: 5 is the SELECTION cut (above it, choose something else), 6 is the RENDER ceiling (above it, the component refuses). Write that distinction down.
s272-D15.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3, then a one-line note on both metas. Datawrapper's 5 is a choice threshold and dv-pie-009's 6 is a drawing limit — they are not actually the same rule, but nothing in the repo says so, so today it reads as a defect.

s272-D16.label: Is a donut better or worse than a pie?

quotes.roles.json (ours): donut is the composition DEFAULT (weight 80); pie is 48
quotes.FT Visual Vocabulary: the centre can be a good way of making space to include more information
quotes.NN/g: made even less effective by the whitespace in the middle
quotes.IBM Carbon: unreachable

options: Keep the ordering: our centre-total discriminator is a REASON, and FT gives the same reason.
Flip it: pie becomes the default and donut is the exception when a centre total earns its place.
Keep the ordering and add NN/g's caution to both metas as a documented dissent.
s272-D16.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. NN/g's objection is to using either for comparison, which our `when` already excludes (composition only, parts sum to a whole). The FT independently reaches our exact discriminator, which is the strongest single corroboration in this slice.

s272-D17.label: When is a bar chart horizontal rather than vertical?

quotes.FT Visual Vocabulary: Good when the data are not time series and labels have long category names
quotes.Datawrapper: If you have more than approximately 10 categories
quotes.IBM Carbon: unreachable
quotes.NN/g: silent
quotes.ours: NO RULE — orientation is a variant with no criterion, and our AP1 only forbids negatives on the horizontal form

options: Adopt the FT test: long category labels or non-time-series ⇒ horizontal.
Adopt the Datawrapper count: > ~10 categories ⇒ horizontal.
Both, ORed — either condition makes it horizontal.
No rule; orientation stays a composer's choice.
s272-D17.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. Both tests are about the same failure — labels that will not fit under a column — and they catch different halves of it. This is the largest completely-absent rule found in the chart family.

s272-D18.label: When does composition-over-time stop being a stacked area and become stacked columns?

quotes.Datawrapper: Area charts work best if you have many dates.
quotes.FT Visual Vocabulary: seeing change in components can be very difficult
quotes.ours: no date count on either side
quotes.IBM Carbon: unreachable

options: Adopt ~10 dates as the cut: fewer ⇒ stacked bar, more ⇒ stacked area.
No number; use "the reader must read individual values" ⇒ stacked bar.
No rule.
s272-D18.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is a single-source number, so it should be ruled the way s270-D1 was — provisional, with a tripwire — but it fills a genuine hole: today a 4-quarter split can legally be drawn as a stacked area, which is the worst option for it.

s272-D19.label: Which intent word gates chart-combo?

quotes.FT Visual Vocabulary: showing the relationship between an amount (columns) and a rate (line)
quotes.FT (filing): listed under CORRELATION first, and again under Change v Time
quotes.roles.json (ours): "two measures in different units over one axis", answers = change-over-time only
quotes.IBM Carbon: the intent buckets exist (Comparisons · Trends · Part-to-whole · Correlations · Connections · Geospatial) but per-chart prose was unreachable
quotes.Datawrapper: has a dual-axis guide but it carries no selection criterion

options: Keep change-over-time only.
Add relationship: answers becomes [change-over-time, relationship], as chart-stacked-area already carries two.
Keep one word and record the FT's second filing as a known gap.
s272-D19.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. chart-stacked-area already proves the two-word pattern is legal on our answers axis, and today a composer whose claim is "revenue against margin rate" is gated to Chart-scatter, which cannot draw it.

s272-D20.label: Which intent word gates the butterfly pair?

quotes.FT (filing): population pyramid is filed under DISTRIBUTION
quotes.roles.json (ours): "exactly two series mirrored, categories ≥ 6", answers = comparison
quotes.everyone else: silent — no other system ships a butterfly

options: Keep comparison only.
Add distribution: answers becomes [comparison, distribution].
Keep comparison and note that a population-pyramid claim must reach it through comparison.
s272-D20.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. Our butterfly's canonical uses are inflow-vs-outflow and actual-vs-target, which are comparisons; the pyramid case is real but rare in fintech, and widening the gate costs more than it buys. Recorded so the decision is visible, not silent.

s272-D21.label: How many colour-coded categories may a legend carry?

quotes.Adobe Spectrum: The ideal usage for these is when there are 8 or fewer categories
quotes.NN/g: color should not be used to communicate information about quantitative
quotes.ours: no ceiling on legend; the isoluminant categorical set's size is a token question
quotes.IBM Carbon: unreachable

options: Adopt 8 as the legend's ceiling.
Rule that the ceiling belongs to the PALETTE (the isoluminant set), not the legend, and point the legend at it.
No ceiling.
s272-D21.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. A legend with 12 entries is not wrong if 12 series are distinguishable; the real constraint is how many isoluminant categorical colours we have. Putting the number on the legend would hide it from the place that determines it.

s272-D22.label: May a Tag be interactive (a link or button)?

quotes.GOV.UK: Do not use tags to create links, buttons or other interactive elements
quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use tags as links that direct you to an entirely different page
quotes.USWDS: Users frequently confuse tags as buttons.
quotes.Ant Design: silent — ships closable and checkable tags without comment
quotes.ours: our meta SHIPS a Tag link variant and only forbids making static tags LOOK interactive

options: Retire the Tag link variant; tags become static labels only.
Keep it but fence it: a Tag link may only filter IN PLACE, never navigate (this is exactly what Carbon's wording leaves open).
Keep it as is and record the three-system disagreement on the meta.
s272-D22.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. Carbon's objection is specifically to NAVIGATION, not to interaction; a removable filter chip is a tag that acts and every system ships one. Option 2 satisfies all three objections without losing a variant we already built.

s272-D23.label: At what wait does a spinner become a progress bar?

quotes.Fluent 2: Progress bars should only be used for tasks that take longer than a second.
quotes.IBM Carbon: If the process takes less than 5 seconds to load, use loading instead
quotes.NN/g: Percent-done animation: Use for actions that take 10 seconds or more.
quotes.Atlassian: For most loading use cases, choose a spinner component.
quotes.Material 3: Choose a loading or progress indicator that corresponds to the expected wait time
quotes.Apple HIG: When possible, use a determinate progress indicator.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: For tasks with a short load time, use the Spinner component
quotes.OURS: loading-indicator.meta antiPatterns[2] (REVIEW, inferred): 'using an indeterminate spinner where a determinate progress bar (known duration) would be clearer' — no number

s272-D23.why_contested: 1s · 5s · 10s · 'most cases use a spinner' · 'whenever possible use determinate'. A 3-second upload is a progress bar at Microsoft, a spinner at IBM, and a spinner at Atlassian. This is the deepest numeric split in the feedback family.
options: Carry NO number. The discriminator is 'is the completion fraction knowable' — if yes, progress bar; if no, spinner. All seven systems can live with this and it is the only clause a gate can actually check.
Adopt Carbon's 5s cut (nearest to our banking upload reality).
Adopt NN/g's research-backed 10s cut and use skeleton or spinner below it.
s272-D23.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. Every number here is a proxy for 'do you know the fraction'. We already state the real test in two metas; naming a second, numeric test would give us two rules that can disagree.

s272-D24.label: How long does a toast stay before auto-dismissing?

quotes.Ant Design: If not specified, default value is 4.5 seconds.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Use to shorten or lengthen the default duration of 5000 milliseconds.
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: Be sure to set a minimum of 5 seconds
quotes.Fluent 2: If there is no action to take, toast will time out after seven seconds.
quotes.Material 3: Snackbars without actions can auto-dismiss after 4-10 seconds, depending on platform.
quotes.Atlassian: silent on duration (states only that critical messages must not auto-dismiss)
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on duration
quotes.GOV.UK: no toast component
quotes.OURS: toast.meta purpose: 'auto-dismisses after ~6s (paused on hover/focus)'

s272-D24.why_contested: Same KIND (a timeout), five different numbers: 4.5 · 5 · 5-min · 7 · 4-10. Ours (6) sits inside every band but matches nobody.
options: Keep ~6s and record it as ruled rather than assumed.
Adopt M3's 4-10s BAND and let the consumer pick inside it by message length.
Adopt Spectrum's shape — a 5s FLOOR with no ceiling, since pause-on-hover already handles slow readers.
s272-D24.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. Our 6s is already built, is inside every external band, and the pause-on-hover we already ship is what actually protects slow readers. This is a cheap ratification, not a change.

s272-D25.label: How many toasts may be on screen at once?

quotes.Material 3: Only one snackbar may be displayed at a time.
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: dismiss, do not show if other toast is present on screen.
quotes.Fluent 2: Don't show more than four toasts in a toaster
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on count
quotes.OURS: toast.meta antiPatterns[4]: 'Stacking unlimited toasts (queue beyond ~3)'

s272-D25.why_contested: Two systems say exactly one; one says four; ours says about three. The KIND agrees (there is a cap) and the NUMBER does not.
options: One at a time (M3 / Spectrum) — the strictest, and the easiest to gate.
Keep ~3 queued.
Cap at 3 but show only ONE at a time, queueing the rest — which satisfies both camps.
s272-D25.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. It is what 'queue beyond ~3' probably already meant, and it makes the gate trivial: assert exactly one toast node in the live region.

s272-D26.label: Is a page-level Banner dismissible?

quotes.Atlassian: Banners should appear one at a time, are not dismissible
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Be dismissible unless they contain critical information or an important step
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: An alert banner should only overlay content if it is dismissible.
quotes.GOV.UK: whether it's sometimes helpful to allow users to dismiss notifications, and how to do this
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on banner dismissal specifically
quotes.OURS: banner.meta antiPatterns[0]: 'Actions AND dismiss on the same banner (family shape rule: either, never both)'

s272-D26.why_contested: Three positions from three systems: never · conditionally · only if it overlays. GOV.UK openly records it as an open research question. Ours answers a different question (either/or) and never answers this one.
options: Banner is never dismissible — it persists until the condition clears (Atlassian). Our either/or rule then collapses to 'actions only'.
Banner is dismissible only when it carries NO action (our existing either/or, made explicit as the answer).
Dismissible unless critical (Polaris) — needs a definition of critical that we do not have.
s272-D26.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 2. It is already our shape rule; it just has not been stated as the answer to this question. Option 3 imports a word ('critical') with no home in our vocabulary.

s272-D27.label: What does a FULL-PAGE load show — spinner or skeleton?

quotes.Adobe Spectrum: Use a progress circle for full page loading or in very small areas.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Not be used to give feedback for an entire page load.
quotes.IBM Carbon: For full-screen loads, skeleton states are preferred over indicators
quotes.Ant Design: Could be replaced by Spin in any situation
quotes.NN/g: Spinners are typically best used on a single module, like a video
quotes.Atlassian: There should only be a single spinner on a page at any time.
quotes.OURS: skeleton-loader.meta: 'use [Loading-indicator] when there is no known layout to mirror' — which does not settle the full-page case, because a page layout IS known

s272-D27.why_contested: Split 2-2 on the identical situation, with Ant saying it does not matter. Our own predicate technically answers 'skeleton' (a page layout is known) but no meta says so and our app-shell templates do not do it.
options: Skeleton for any full-page or full-region load where the layout is known (Carbon / Polaris / NN/g); spinner reserved for single modules.
Spinner for full-page, skeleton for in-page regions (Spectrum).
Either, by template — declared per app-shell rather than globally.
s272-D27.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. It follows from the predicate we already have rather than adding a new one, and Polaris's flat prohibition on page-load spinners is the strongest single statement in the row.

s272-D28.label: Below what wait is a skeleton worse than nothing?

quotes.NN/g: they are best used when the page takes 2-10 seconds to load
quotes.Ant Design: When a resource needs long time to load.
quotes.IBM Carbon: should only appear for only a few seconds, disappearing once components and
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Be used for pages where all content loads at the same time.
quotes.OURS: skeleton-loader.meta antiPatterns[5]: 'Skeleton for sub-300ms loads (flash of placeholder is worse than nothing)'

s272-D28.why_contested: Our floor is 300ms. NN/g's band starts at 2 seconds — nearly seven times higher. Between 300ms and 2s our library shows a skeleton and NN/g shows nothing.
options: Keep 300ms (a flash-prevention threshold, which is what it really is).
Raise to NN/g's 2s (a perceived-performance threshold).
Keep 300ms as the DELAY before the skeleton appears, and adopt 10s as the point where it must hand over to a progress bar — two different jobs, two different numbers.
s272-D28.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. Our 300ms and NN/g's 2s are answering different questions; option 3 keeps both without contradiction and adds the upper handover NN/g gives us for free.

s272-D29.label: What must a confirmation screen contain?

quotes.GOV.UK: Your confirmation page must include: a reference number, if there is one
quotes.GOV.UK (2): Some users will bookmark the confirmation page as a form of receipt.
quotes.Ant Design: Use when important operations need to inform the user to process the results
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on required contents
quotes.OURS: confirmation.meta: 'a success-solid glyph, a heading, a short message and the next actions'

s272-D29.why_contested: GOV.UK gives a six-item MUST list (reference number, what happens next and when, contact details, onward links, feedback link, a way to save a record) and raises a case nobody else does — the bookmarked receipt. Ours names four items, none of them a reference number. For a payment confirmation the reference number is the whole point.
options: Adopt GOV.UK's must-list wholesale.

Adopt the banking-relevant subset: reference number (when one exists), what happens next and when, and a way to save or print. Drop the feedback link, which is a GOV.UK service-assessment requirement, not a banking one.
Keep our four items and record the divergence.
s272-D29.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 2. A payment confirmation without a reference is unusable in a dispute, and 'a way to save a record' is what the bookmark behaviour is really asking for. The feedback link genuinely does not transfer.

s272-D30.label: Must an empty state always offer an action?

quotes.Atlassian: Include an action or link to help people understand what to do next.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Empty states are used when a list, table, or chart has no items
quotes.Ant Design: When there is no data provided, display for friendly tips.
quotes.IBM Carbon: For simpler situations, or for secondary features where bite-sized pieces of information are preferable.
quotes.GOV.UK: no empty-state component
quotes.NN/g: not obtained — the article slug tried 404'd (see SOURCES refused)
quotes.OURS: empty-state.meta: three postures — first-run (primary button), no-results (link), quiet (say so and stop)

s272-D30.why_contested: Atlassian says always give the reader something to press. Our 'quiet' posture deliberately gives nothing. Nobody outside has our three-posture split, so there is no external support for the quiet case either.
options: Keep all three postures; quiet stays actionless.
Drop the quiet posture; every empty region offers at least a link.
Keep quiet but fence it: legal only where the emptiness is GOOD NEWS (inbox caught up, no overdue payments) and not where the user could create the missing thing.
s272-D30.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. It preserves the distinction that makes our empty-state better than the imports while answering Atlassian's real worry — a dead end where an action was possible.

s272-D31.label: Must an error Alert carry an action?

quotes.Fluent 2: Error and Warning messages must have either a link to content or a button
quotes.Atlassian: The message is restricted to five lines in length.
quotes.NN/g: Display the error message close to the error's source.
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on a required action
quotes.GOV.UK: silent on a required action (its error summary links to the fields, which is an action of a kind)
quotes.OURS: alert.meta: 'title + description + optional inline link + optional dismiss' — the link is OPTIONAL

s272-D31.why_contested: One system makes the action mandatory for errors and warnings; ours makes it optional; the rest are silent. It matters because an error with no route out is the most common real failure in the family.
options: Adopt Fluent's rule: an error or warning Alert must carry either a link or a button.
Keep optional, but require that the DESCRIPTION states what to do next (NN/g's actual concern, met with copy rather than a control).
Keep as written.
s272-D31.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 2. It satisfies the underlying concern without forcing a control onto errors whose fix is simply 'try again later', and it is checkable by the copy gate rather than the component gate.

s272-D32.label: Does `notifications` keep a catalogue identity, or become a pointer?

quotes.IBM Carbon: For more context on when to use each notification variant, including modals,
quotes.NN/g: Notifications are focused on system-related events.
quotes.NN/g (2): Validations are tied to a user's action or input.
quotes.Ant Design: A notification with complex content.
quotes.Atlassian: For messages that appear after an event takes place, use a flag.
quotes.GOV.UK: no umbrella component — notification banner, error summary and error message are separate
quotes.OURS: notifications.meta describes four placements — Contextual, Global, Inline, Snackbar — which ARE Alert, Banner, inline validation and Toast

s272-D32.why_contested: Not a disagreement about a rule but about an IDENTITY. Our library has four Mono feedback components plus a Legacy record that describes all four again. Externally, Carbon keeps an umbrella and NN/g cuts by trigger instead of placement — neither maps onto our four placements.
options: Notifications keeps its catalogue identity as the Legacy record and gains a `when` of 'never — see Alert / Banner / Toast / inline validation'.
Notifications is retired from the catalogue; its slug redirects to the three Mono components.
Notifications is re-cut along NN/g's trigger axis (indicator / validation / notification), which would re-shape all four Mono components.
s272-D32.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. It costs nothing, keeps the Legacy name findable for anyone arriving from the old toolkit, and stops a fifth door opening into the same four rooms. Option 2 loses the search term; option 3 re-opens components that #268 already shipped.

s272-D33.label: Are alias metas exempt from a when-completeness gate?

quotes.ours (s210-D5): progress-bar.meta.json and limits-meter.meta.json are thin category aliases of meter.meta.json; writing spec into them is an antiPattern
quotes.ours (this harvest): any gate requiring a `when` on every meta would FORCE that breach

options: Exempt aliases explicitly: the gate reads the parent's `when`.
Allow a `when` on an alias only if it is a verbatim pointer to the parent.
Do not build a when-completeness gate at all.
s272-D33.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is the only option that keeps s210-D5 intact. Flagged here because it must be decided BEFORE any `when` lands as a gated field, not after.

s272-D34.label: countdown-timer
s272-D34.when_gate: a timed event will fire without the user AND the remaining time is available as TEXT, not only as a ring AND the user can extend or dismiss the limit
s272-D34.when_prose: not a choice between siblings but a disclosure: it rides inside Banner, Modals, a session-timeout prompt or Secure-entry's resend; the extend clause is our antiPatterns[1] and it is really WCAG 2.2.1 wearing a component's clothes; never appears in a cta-lockup, where our own meta calls a countdown manufactured urgency.

s272-D35.label: Must a Stat card carry a delta?

quotes.ours (meta when): shape = one-measure × value-and-delta AND series = none AND delta != none
quotes.roles.json (ours): "default — label · value · delta · period, no series"
quotes.Ant Design: When want to display statistic data with description.
quotes.IBM Carbon: Use tiles to group related information in flexible containers.

options: Yes, delta required. A bare number is not a Stat card and needs a named home.
No: delta becomes optional and the gate drops to "one measure, no series".
Yes, required — and account-card becomes the named home for a bare balance.
s272-D35.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. It keeps the role's fences intact (no series ⇒ not a KPI tile; no delta ⇒ not a Stat card) and it gives the bare-number case a real destination instead of leaving it homeless. Ant's Statistic shows the alternative design and it is looser than ours by a long way.

s272-D36.label: Is a slider legal in a form at all?

quotes.GOV.UK: Avoid using range slider questions, where the user needs to click and drag
quotes.Fluent 2: Use a slider for imprecise values.
quotes.Atlassian: Don't use a range if choosing a specific value is important.
quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use for extremely large ranges, for example, 1-1000.
quotes.Material 3: Changes made with sliders must take effect immediately
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: used when the upper and lower bounds to the range are invariable.
quotes.NN/g: Sliders or knobs are continuous controls.
quotes.Apple HIG: Consider supplementing a slider with a corresponding text field and stepper.
quotes.USWDS: no slider component
quotes.OURS: slider.meta antiPatterns[2] (REVIEW, inferred): 'using a slider where precise numeric entry is required (pair with an input)'

s272-D36.why_contested: GOV.UK rejects the interaction outright on accessibility grounds (WCAG 2.5.1 pointer gestures) and ships no slider. Six systems ship one with conditions. M3 adds a condition none of the others do: the change must take effect immediately — which would make a slider inside a submitted form illegal.
options: Slider is legal in filters and settings only, never inside a submitted form (M3's immediacy test, and it sidesteps most of GOV.UK's objection since filters re-apply live).
Slider is legal anywhere, always paired with a linked numeric field (NN/g and Apple HIG both require the pairing).
Slider is removed from the input role and kept only as a display/filter control.
Slider stands as built; record the GOV.UK divergence.
s272-D36.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1 plus the pairing from option 2 wherever a value is committed. The immediacy test is the same test that separates Switch from Checkbox in s270 — one predicate, two families, which is worth more than a slider-specific rule.

s272-D37.label: For a date the user already knows (date of birth, card expiry): calendar picker or three plain text boxes?

quotes.GOV.UK: a date they'll already know, or can look up without using a calendar
quotes.GOV.UK (dates pattern): Only use a calendar control if users need to: pick a date
quotes.Shopify Polaris: always give users the option to enter the date using a text field component
quotes.USWDS: Always allow a user to type in the date manually
quotes.Atlassian: For most situations, use the date picker or date time picker components
quotes.Material 3: Text field drop-downs on medium and expanded breakpoints like tablet and desktop
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on the choice (size guidance only)
quotes.OURS: date-picker.meta: a boxed field with free typing PLUS a panel from the tail button; calendar.meta antiPatterns[0] draws the read-vs-pick line

s272-D37.why_contested: GOV.UK restricts the calendar control to near/relational dates and uses three text boxes for everything else. Four other systems treat the calendar panel as the default with typing as a fallback. A date of birth gets two different components depending on which system you follow.
options: Date-picker everywhere, typing always available (our current build; matches Atlassian, M3, Carbon, Ant).

Split by date class: memorable/known dates (DOB, card expiry) get plain fields; chosen dates (payment date, appointment) get Date-picker. This is GOV.UK's rule and it is checkable from the field's semantics.
Date-picker everywhere, but the panel does not open for known-date fields.
s272-D37.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 2. It is the only one backed by named research, it costs us nothing we have built (the typed field already exists and already validates on blur), and 'is this date one the user knows' is a question the form author can always answer.

s272-D38.label: Is a clickable multi-step progress indicator legal at all?

quotes.GOV.UK: Do not use progress indicators that do all of the following:
quotes.USWDS: has fewer than three sections, don't use a step indicator.
quotes.Atlassian: Use a progress tracker for more detailed journeys spanning multiple screens.
quotes.IBM Carbon: When a process or form has fewer than three steps.
quotes.Ant Design: we can decompose it into several steps to make things easier.
quotes.OURS: stepper.meta: 'back-navigation on completed dots' plus 'Clickable FUTURE steps' as antiPatterns[0]

s272-D38.why_contested: GOV.UK forbids the exact COMBINATION our Stepper implements — all steps shown, previous steps navigable, current step marked — and cites a service that removed a 12-step tracker with no effect on completion. Four other systems ship that combination happily.
options: Stepper stands as built; record the divergence from GOV.UK in the meta.
Stepper drops back-navigation on completed dots, leaving a Back button as the only route — which lands us outside GOV.UK's prohibition.
Stepper stands, but only above N steps (GOV.UK's objection is loudest for long forms; USWDS, Carbon and Atlassian all put the floor at 3).
s272-D38.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3 with the floor at 3. The floor is unanimous among the three systems that name one, and it neutralises most of GOV.UK's objection without removing a feature we have already built and tested.

s272-D39.label: What is the maximum number of steps in a flow?

quotes.Atlassian (progress-tracker): If a task needs more than six steps, consider simplifying the process
quotes.Atlassian (progress-indicator): Use a maximum of seven steps in your journey so that people aren't overwhelmed.
quotes.Fluent 2: Drawers allow for multi-step tasks, but should be kept to two to three steps.
quotes.USWDS: silent on a maximum
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on a maximum
quotes.GOV.UK: cites a 12-step tracker removed with no effect on completion rates or times
quotes.OURS: silent

s272-D39.why_contested: The same system gives two different ceilings on two pages. Fluent gives a third, much lower one, but only for a drawer. Most systems give none.
options: No ceiling — the number of steps is the journey's business, not the component's.
Six (Atlassian's progress-tracker page — the stricter of its two).
No ceiling on the flow, but a ceiling of 3 on a flow inside a DRAWER or MODAL (Fluent's actual point).
s272-D39.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. The evidence for a general ceiling is one system contradicting itself; the evidence for a ceiling inside a constrained surface is specific and matches what our own Modals/Drawer metas already worry about.

s272-D40.label: What range is too small or too large for a slider?

quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use for extremely large ranges, for example, 1-1000.
quotes.IBM Carbon (2): Do not use ranges that are too small, for example, 1-3.
quotes.Atlassian: Don't use for ranges that are very small (for example, 1-3).
quotes.Atlassian (2): Don't use for ranges that are extremely large.
quotes.OURS: silent

s272-D40.why_contested: Two systems agree exactly on the lower bound (1-3) and both hedge the upper one — Carbon offers 1-1000 as an EXAMPLE, not a rule; Atlassian gives no number at all.
options: Adopt the lower bound only: under ~5 discrete steps use selection-controls instead. Leave the upper bound to judgement.
Adopt both, with 1-1000 as the stated upper example.
Carry no bounds and rely on the imprecision test alone (R-A-14).
s272-D40.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. The lower bound is the only genuinely agreed number in this row, and it hands the excluded cases straight to a component we already have.

s272-D41.label: One file per input, or a staged list of files against one dropzone?

quotes.USWDS: Prefer one file per input.
quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use upload in a modal when multiple files are uploaded
quotes.Ant Design: When you need to upload files by dragging and dropping.
quotes.GOV.UK: You should only ask users to upload something if it's critical to the delivery
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Provide feedback once the file(s) have been dropped and uploading begins.
quotes.OURS: file-upload.meta: 'a dashed dropzone … staging files into rows with per-file determinate progress'

s272-D41.why_contested: USWDS states a preference our component structurally cannot honour — we stage a list. Carbon fences multi-file upload out of modals. Nobody else takes a position.
options: Multi-file staging stays the default; record the USWDS divergence.
One file per input is the default, with a declared multi-file variant for evidence journeys (dispute evidence, mortgage documents) where a list is genuinely the job.
Multi-file staging stays, plus Carbon's fence: file-upload never appears inside a Modal.
s272-D41.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. USWDS's preference is about error clarity, which our per-file error rows already solve; Carbon's fence names a real failure (a growing list inside a fixed-height dialog) that our Modals meta does not currently forbid.

s272-D42.label: Do we carry a file-size cap, and what is it?

quotes.Shopify Polaris: File size must be less than 20MB
quotes.GOV.UK: silent on a number
quotes.USWDS: silent on a number
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on a number
quotes.Ant Design: silent on a number
quotes.OURS: silent — antiPatterns[2] requires a visible error for an oversize file but names no size

s272-D42.why_contested: Exactly one system in eleven gives a number. Our meta requires the oversize ERROR without defining oversize, which means the rule cannot be tested.
options: Carry no number; the cap is the consuming service's and must be stated in the field's help text.
Adopt a library default (Polaris's 20MB) that a service may lower.
Carry no number but GATE the presence of a stated limit in the help text — the rule becomes 'a limit must be visible', not 'the limit is N'.
s272-D42.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. A number picked from one system would be arbitrary; 'the limit must be visible before the user picks a file' is the part that actually prevents the failure our antiPattern describes.

s272-D43.label: Is a segmented per-digit OTP field right, or should the code be one field?

quotes.USWDS: Avoid breaking numbers with distinct sections into separate input fields.
quotes.Apple HIG: Use secure text fields to hide private data.
quotes.GOV.UK: no segmented-code component (its password-input is a single field with a reveal)
quotes.IBM Carbon: no segmented-code component
quotes.OURS: secure-entry.meta: 'per-digit cells with auto-advance, backspace step-back, whole-code paste, verify-on-fill'

s272-D43.why_contested: One system states a principle that directly contradicts the component's form; ten ship nothing comparable. It is one-against-silence, not one-against-many — but the one is a government accessibility authority and the objection is specific.
options: Secure-entry stands; record the USWDS divergence and lean on our own per-digit announcement and paste support as the mitigations.
Secure-entry becomes one field with a format hint, keeping paste and verify-on-fill and losing the cells.
Secure-entry stands for OTP (where paste is the happy path and the code is machine-generated) and is forbidden for anything the user recalls from memory.
s272-D43.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. USWDS's objection is about splitting a number the USER KNOWS across boxes; an SMS code is pasted, not recalled. The distinction is real, checkable, and it keeps the component we have built.

s272-D44.label: One question per page, or grouped multi-field forms?

quotes.GOV.UK: Asking just one question per question page helps users understand what you're asking
quotes.NN/g: Users now see a 3-part form with 4-6 fields.
quotes.IBM Carbon: If a form has more than one column, then the columns should be proportional and
quotes.Fluent 2: By default, field labels are top-aligned above the form component.
quotes.OURS: form-layout.meta: 'proximity-grouped field pairs' — i.e. multi-field by design

s272-D44.why_contested: GOV.UK's one-thing-per-page is a whole service-design posture, not a component rule; NN/g and Carbon assume grouped multi-field forms. Our Form-layout is built for the latter and our Stepper exists to split long ones.
options: Multi-field grouped forms stay the default; one-thing-per-page is available via Stepper for high-stakes journeys (payments, onboarding).
One question per page becomes the default for any journey that moves money.
No rule — leave density to the journey.
s272-D44.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. It describes what we have already built, and it gives the GOV.UK posture a named home (Stepper) rather than leaving it as an unattributed contradiction in the docs.

s272-D45.label: Does the predictive-search dropdown belong to Search-field or to Combobox?

quotes.USWDS: Use a combo box when there are more than 15 choices
quotes.Material 3: Use a search icon button when search is a secondary action
quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use when there is small or limited amounts of data.
quotes.Adobe Spectrum: silent on the overlap (search-field and combo-box are separate pages with no cross-reference)
quotes.OURS: search-field.meta claims 'an optional predictive-search (autocomplete) dropdown'; combobox.meta claims 'A text input that filters a list of options as the user types, and commits one of them'

s272-D45.why_contested: NOT AN EXTERNAL DISAGREEMENT — an internal one. Two of our metas describe a text field over a filtered list, with the same ARIA contract, under two names. No external system resolves it because none ships both with overlapping scope.
options: Split by COMMIT: combobox commits a value into a form; search-field hands a query to a result set and commits nothing. The predictive dropdown moves to combobox.
Split by TARGET: search-field searches CONTENT, combobox selects a VALUE — same outcome, different words.
Merge: one component with a commit-or-query mode.
s272-D45.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. 'Does a value land in the form' is machine-checkable; 'is it content or a value' is not. This also keeps Command-palette clean, since it commits a command rather than a value.

s272-D46.label: What does a SUPERSEDED component's `when` say?

quotes.ours (filter-toolbar-bar AP1): Consuming View-options instead of Segmented-control for the view switch — View-options was superseded 2026-07-24
quotes.ours (view-options meta): reads as a live recommendation: "A view control that lets users select different presentation formats"

options: Give it a `when` that says "never — use Segmented-control".
Remove it from the library.
Leave it and rely on filter-toolbar-bar's antiPattern to catch misuse.
s272-D46.lane_recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. Option 3 is the status quo and it failed once already — the supersession is recorded on a DIFFERENT component's antiPattern, where nobody choosing a view switch would look.

s272-D47.label: date-range-picker
s272-D47.when_gate: the answer is TWO dates that bound one period AND both endpoints share ONE calendar panel AND an out-of-order pair errors rather than silently swapping
s272-D47.when_prose: beats two Date-pickers side by side (our own antiPatterns[0]: "Two independent single-date pickers with no shared panel or cross-field check") because order errors otherwise surface too late; beats date-picker whenever the question is a statement period, a transaction search window or a custom reporting window; yields to date-picker whenever only one date is asked for.

s272-D48.label: tags-input
s272-D48.when_gate: the committed values are the USER'S OWN words AND no option list can be offered AND each value becomes a removable Tags chip AND a half-typed value is committed on blur, never discarded
s272-D48.when_prose: beats combobox (#270: "options >= 16, closed list") and multi-select (#270: "the answer is a set") on the single test our meta already states — is there a list at all; where a list exists the answer belongs to one of those two, and where it does not, only this component is honest (it explicitly does not claim role=combobox without a list, our antiPatterns[3]); the chip itself is the gated Tags atom, so any chip change lands in Tags first.

s272-D49.label: secure-entry
s272-D49.when_gate: the value is a one-time code or PIN of known length AND each digit has its own cell AND whole-code paste is accepted AND the result of verify-on-fill reaches a live region
s272-D49.when_prose: beats input-fields (proposed "free text, one line") for OTP and PIN only, because the per-digit cells buy per-digit announcement and the resend countdown belongs to the same contract; never blocks paste, which is the OTP happy path (our antiPatterns[1]); yields to input-fields for a password, which is a secure field but not a segmented one (Apple HIG: "Use secure text fields to hide private data").

s272-D50.label: account-selector
s272-D50.when_gate: role = input AND options = accounts (name + masked number + balance) AND the payment flow needs a from or a to
s272-D50.when_prose: beats dropdown (#270 proposed: "6–15 options and the column cannot spare the height") because the option rows are RICH and a raw select for the same choice is on our mustNotNeighbour list; the compact chip form is the CHOSEN state inline, not a second control.

s272-D51.label: May a tooltip contain interactive content?

quotes.Material 3: Rich tooltips can have up to two text buttons.
quotes.IBM Carbon: Do not use interactive elements within a tooltip.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Not contain any links or buttons.
quotes.Fluent 2: Tooltips should be used to provide helpful but non-essential, plaintext information.
quotes.Atlassian: Don't put critical task information in a tooltip
quotes.NN/g: Don't use tooltips for information that is vital to task completion.
quotes.USWDS: Don't use a tooltip if you need a lot of text.
quotes.OURS: tooltip.meta antiPatterns[1]: 'Putting essential information or interactive elements only inside a tooltip'

s272-D51.why_contested: Ten sources say no; M3 says yes and calls it a rich tooltip. M3 has effectively merged tooltip and popover — a merge we have explicitly rejected by shipping both.
options: No interactive content in a tooltip, full stop. M3's rich tooltip maps onto our Popover.
Follow M3 and allow up to two text buttons, collapsing Popover into Tooltip.
s272-D51.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1, and it is nearly free — our own popover.meta already states the three-way rule that makes M3's rich tooltip a Popover in our vocabulary. This row exists only so the M3 divergence is recorded rather than discovered later.

s272-D52.label: Are Drawer and Modals' 'Partial modal' the same component — and does Drawer survive?

quotes.Atlassian: We are planning on deprecating Drawer. Please use Modal instead.
quotes.Material 3: Modal side sheets are preferred in compact breakpoints, like mobile
quotes.Apple HIG: Display only one sheet at a time from the main interface.
quotes.Ant Design: When subtasks are too heavy for a Popover
quotes.IBM Carbon: silent on drawer (no such component)
quotes.OURS: drawer.meta: a page-edge side sheet; modals.meta ALSO describes 'Partial modal / Drawer (app-only, anchored to the bottom of the screen)'

s272-D52.why_contested: This is a defect before it is a disagreement: two of our own metas describe the same surface under two names. Externally, one system is removing the component entirely while three defend it, and M3 makes its modality depend on breakpoint where ours does not.
options: One Drawer component with an edge parameter (left/right/bottom); Modals' partial-modal text is removed and points at it.
Two components: Drawer (side, desktop) and Partial modal (bottom, mobile) — with a stated reason why they are not one thing.
Fold Drawer into Modals as a placement variant (Atlassian's direction).
s272-D52.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 1. The mechanics our two metas describe are identical — scrim, trap, inert, Esc, focus return — and the only difference is which edge it docks to. That is a parameter, not a component.

s272-D53.label: At what size does a popover become a drawer or a modal?

quotes.IBM Carbon: If your popover exceeds four columns in width, use a modal instead.
quotes.Fluent 2: Content in popovers should never be essential for someone to complete a task.
quotes.Shopify Polaris: Be used for secondary or less important information and actions since they're hidden
quotes.Apple HIG: Show one popover at a time.
quotes.OURS: popover.meta antiPatterns[2]: 'Popover content that scrolls (too much content — use a Drawer or Modal)'

s272-D53.why_contested: The KIND is agreed — a popover has an upper size limit — but only Carbon gives a measurable one. Ours and Atlassian's use scrolling as a proxy, which is a consequence rather than a threshold.
options: Keep the scroll test (ours + Atlassian). Simple, but it can only be checked at runtime.
Adopt Carbon's four-column cut, translated into our grid.
Both: the scroll test as the rule, the column cut as the design-time guide.
s272-D53.lane_recommendation: LANE'S RECOMMENDATION: option 3. The scroll test catches the real failure; the column figure is what a designer can actually use before the content exists.

s272-D54.label: modal-lightbox
